claims.text: The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static compressive strength of 1314 MPa.
The starting HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static fracture strain of 13.5%.
Optimized aging after hot working can produce a homogeneous dispersion of nanoscale B2-ordered precipitates in HfZrTiTa0.53.
The proposed B2 precipitates will be thermally stable under the relevant dynamic-deformation conditions.
Nanoscale B2 precipitates will impede dislocation motion.
Impediment of dislocation motion by the B2 precipitates will promote dynamic strain hardening.
The B2 precipitate dispersion will increase activation of multiple slip systems.
The B2 precipitates will obstruct shear-band propagation and suppress strain localization.
Suppression of strain localization will delay dynamic failure.
The intervention will increase yield strength by approximately 10–15% relative to the baseline.
The intervention will increase compressive strength relative to the baseline.
The intervention will increase strain to failure by approximately 30–40% relative to the baseline.
The intervention will improve uniform deformation and resistance to strain localization.
Under dynamic loading, the intervention will make impact-induced energy release more gradual.
More gradual impact-induced energy release will correspond to improved energy absorption.
The predicted improvements apply primarily under adiabatic dynamic deformation at strain rates exceeding approximately 10^3 s^-1.
The effects of the precipitate dispersion on strain hardening and localization may be less pronounced at lower strain rates or under isothermal conditions.
